[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood here, I'll kick us off. Uh, quickly do intros -- Maya from SE, Liam from CSM, and from Aurora?
[00:12] Rachel Kim: Rachel Kim, VP Legal. Hi all.
[00:15] David Ortiz: David Ortiz, procurement.
[00:18] Anita Rao: Anita, security engineering.
[00:21] Marcus Lee: Marcus, CTO, sorry I'm a few minutes late.
[00:30] Samir Patel: No worries Marcus, glad you could make it. Quick agenda -- we want to run through the MSA/DPA redlines you sent, align on SLA expectations for Dedicated, review required security artifacts (SOC2, network diagram, KMS), and outline next steps for procurement and onboarding. Sound good?
[00:45] Rachel Kim: Yes, that's perfect. We did send redlines yesterday. We're mostly focused on data processing clauses and audit rights in the DPA.
[00:53] Maya Chen: Cool, Rachel. On the DPA specifics, can you call out the clauses you're most concerned about? We might have standard responses but we want to be specific.
[01:05] Rachel Kim: Yeah, section 4.2 -- subprocessor disclosures. We want prior notice and 30-day right to object. Also retention and deletion timing -- we asked for 30 days after termination.
[01:18] Samir Patel: Understood. Our typical is 60 days for deletion for hosted, but for Dedicated we can do 30 with contractual language for customer-managed keys. We'll flag that as negotiable.
[01:30] David Ortiz: On the procurement side, budget approvals are stuck until we have firm pricing for Dedicated. Can you share the 3-node SKU and expected monthly run rate? Also any one-time onboarding fees?
[01:42] Maya Chen: Yes -- we'll send a pricing sheet after the call. Roughly for a Dedicated 3-GPU pool with N nodes it's X per month -- I'll put exact numbers and a breakdown of tokens/throughput in the sheet. There is a one-time onboarding setup fee which covers onboarding and runbook -- we'll itemize.
[01:58] Anita Rao: Security -- we need certified SOC 2 Type II and a recent pen test. Also SSO via SAML and RBAC that maps to our IdP groups. Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[02:12] Maya Chen: We support SSO/SAML and RBAC; mapping Okta groups is common. For KMS -- yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private deployments is supported, and we can document the integration.
[02:24] Marcus Lee: Network -- we require VPC peering or private link. Is that available for Dedicated?
[02:29] Samir Patel: Dedicated can be deployed into a customer VPC or connected via private link; we'll include a network diagram and options.
[02:36] Rachel Kim: On audit rights -- we prefer on-site audit rights, but may accept a third-party SOC review + evidence package.
[02:43] Samir Patel: We generally provide SOC2 reports and an audit package; on-site audits are rare for hosted customers but for Dedicated/Private we can discuss more direct audit arrangements.
[02:52] David Ortiz: Timeline -- we're aiming to get vendor approval by 9/20 so legal and procurement need finalized redlines by 9/9. Is that feasible?
[02:59] Samir Patel: Yes, if we get your redlines consolidated we'll have legal respond within 48-72 hours and we can iterate. We'll aim to have a final MSA/DPA exchange completed by 9/12 to give you time for approvals.
[03:10] Maya Chen: On SLA numbers -- Aurora wants 99.9% uptime and p99 latency under 2 seconds for text generation at typical payloads. For a Dedicated 3-node pool we can commit to an SLA of 99.9% with clearly defined maintenance windows and a p99 guidance; p99 under 2s will depend on request mix. We can add an SLO with credits for breaches.
[03:34] Anita Rao: We need specifics on maintenance windows and notification cadence.
[03:38] Liam O'Connor: We'll include standard maintenance policy: notified 72 hours for scheduled maintenance and emergency maintenance less than that with postmortem. Also we can add canary rollout language for model updates.
[03:51] Marcus Lee: What about fallback if a Dedicated region goes down? Is there automatic routing to hosted backup or another region?
[03:58] Maya Chen: Smart routing is supported; we can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model in another region or to Redwood-hosted pool under pre-agreed terms. That would be part of the runbook and routing policy.
[04:12] David Ortiz: Pricing approvals -- procurement needs line-item costs and validation that we won't exceed monthly commit without explicit approval. Also want a cap-on-billing clause.
[04:22] Samir Patel: We'll add usage thresholds and alerts; overage policy requires approval, and we can include a hard cap option if you want.
[04:30] Rachel Kim: On data residency and DPA -- Aurora processes EU customer data; we need commitments about where data is processed and subprocessor list -- particularly any third-party cloud providers.
[04:42] Maya Chen: We have region-specific deployments and can guarantee data residency in EU regions for Dedicated. We'll provide a subprocessor list and be transparent about cloud infra.
[04:51] Anita Rao: Encryption -- at-rest and in-transit; we need keys rotated every 90 days and support for bring-your-own-key.
[04:59] Maya Chen: BYOK supported, rotation cadence can be a contractual requirement. We'll confirm the rotation options with our security docs.
[05:07] Rachel Kim: Liability caps -- we've redlined to ask for higher caps for breach related to data processing. Is there flexibility?
[05:15] Samir Patel: Typically standard caps are tied to 12 months' fees; enterprise deals can negotiate higher caps. We'll have legal follow up on that.
[05:22] David Ortiz: Procurement note -- our PO process requires a signed MSA and an initial invoice schedule. Also need the W-9 and vendor forms.
[05:30] Liam O'Connor: We'll attach vendor forms and W-9 after signature. Invoices can be monthly or quarterly as you prefer.
[05:36] Marcus Lee: Onboarding cadence -- we want to start on technical onboarding as soon as legal signs. How long does the onboarding usually take?
[05:44] Maya Chen: For Dedicated 3-node it's typically 2-3 weeks for initial setup and performance tuning; initial integration work (SSO, network, KMS) runs in parallel.
[05:52] Rachel Kim: Can you provide a runbook and an escalation contact list?
[05:55] Liam O'Connor: Yes, runbook and escalation matrix will be shared during onboarding. We'll include escalation levels and SLA credit process.
[06:03] David Ortiz: On contract terms -- do you have standard 12 month or 36 month agreements? We might prefer 12 with an option to renew.
[06:10] Samir Patel: Standard is 12 months for Dedicated with multi-year discounts available. We'll include renewal and termination terms.
[06:18] Anita Rao: For compliance, can we get a pen test report redacted?
[06:22] Maya Chen: We can share a redacted pen test and a SOC2 report. We'll include that in the security package.
[06:29] Rachel Kim: Great. Also, can Redwood accept a limited SLA credit cap rather than refunds?
[06:34] Samir Patel: Yes, SLA credits are the common remedy and we'll put that in the SLA language.
[06:39] David Ortiz: Procurement question -- any preferred payment methods? ACH or wire is fine, but can you accept Net 30?
[06:46] Samir Patel: Net 30 is standard for enterprise; we'll note that in the quote.
[06:50] Marcus Lee: Any known integrations for our observability stack (we use Datadog)?
[06:54] Maya Chen: We have Datadog metrics + tracing hooks, and you can export token-level cost and latency breakdowns. We'll include example dashboards.
[07:03] Rachel Kim: Ok moving toward wrap up -- to confirm action items: redlines by 9/9, security docs and SOC2 by Redwood by 9/10, pricing sheet by 9/10, onboarding call scheduled for 9/14.
[07:15] Samir Patel: Yes. Anything else?
[07:18] Marcus Lee: Just to confirm the fallback routing option cost implications -- include that in the pricing.
[07:22] Maya Chen: Will do.
[07:24] David Ortiz: Also, send a versioned MSA + DPA PDF with change tracking if possible. Makes review easier.
[07:30] Samir Patel: Absolutely, we'll send tracked changes.
[07:33] Rachel Kim: Thanks everyone, that covers it.
[07:36] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[07:40] Samir Patel: Thanks team -- end.
